findings.title: Findings converge on the shared pipeline stage as the place where author, subject and level are decided
findings.why_it_matters: Author, subject stamp and level gate are all placed in a downstream QueueHandler-stage pipeline that cannot see dropped records, lacks resource knowledge, misses Phase 1, and lets ambient context override the writing logger.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate where author, subject and level are decided (the shared QueueHandler-stage pipeline or the writing logger) before addressing Findings 2, 3, 7 and 8 individually.
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate where author, subject and level are decided (the shared QueueHandler-stage pipeline or the writing logger) before addressing Findings 2, 3, 7 and 8 individually.
findings.choice_reason: Adopted: identity on logger objects at construction, thin ancestor resolver on both handlers, owner wins, framework_log_level as plain logger levels, no gate.

findings.title: D4's subject-aware gate can't work as a pipeline filter, because the logger level drops records before any filter runs
findings.why_it_matters: stdlib checks isEnabledFor before filters, so a downstream gate never sees DEBUG records from INFO loggers.
findings.recommended: A: Per-child logger level, plus a gate only on shared loggers
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D1 and D3 don't say how an app's own logger and the owning app are identified
findings.why_it_matters: The pipeline has no resource knowledge and would have to parse logger names or duplicate a registry.
findings.recommended: A: Stamp author and owner on the writing logger at construction
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D2 doesn't name the framework-owned logger that lifecycle lines move to
findings.why_it_matters: Generic lifecycle code logs through resource.logger; without a named framework logger D2's correct-by-construction claim is unsupported.
findings.recommended: A: D2 names a per-resource sibling framework logger, stamped as framework with the app as owner, and the lifecycle, operations, service and task_bucket sites move to it.
findings.chosen: A: D2 names a per-resource sibling framework logger, stamped as framework with the app as owner, and the lifecycle, operations, service and task_bucket sites move to it.
findings.choice_reason: Resolved as part of the Finding 1 placement the user adopted (per-app lifecycle logger).

findings.title: D8 gives source_tier two meanings under one name
findings.why_it_matters: source_tier is owner tier on registrations and would be author on logs, silently, under one shared literal.
findings.recommended: A: Add a log-only `author` attribute, column and query parameter. `source_tier` keeps meaning owner tier on registrations and stops being fed into the log filter. #739 still closes, since `app_key` stays.
findings.chosen: A: Add a log-only `author` attribute, column and query parameter. `source_tier` keeps meaning owner tier on registrations and stops being fed into the log filter. #739 still closes, since `app_key` stays.

findings.title: The default global Logs view and bare hassette log stop showing framework-authored lines about apps
findings.why_it_matters: Lifecycle and inferred-app framework lines would vanish from the default global view; D9 only set per-app defaults.
findings.recommended: B: D9 states that the global default is "lines about any app, or written by any app", marked by author, in both the UI and the CLI. The tier filter can still narrow to author only.
findings.chosen: U1: Hide framework everywhere, opt-in
findings.choice_reason: User wanted one rule on every page and command rather than per-view defaults; peers checked (none use a composite default).

findings.title: Phase 1 and Phase 2 read identity from different sources
findings.why_it_matters: Only Phase 2 has CorrelationFilter; Phase 1 uses ambient context.
findings.recommended: A: State in D3 and D7 that the identity stamp runs where both phases see it
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D3's context wins lets inherited ambient context override the writing logger's owner
findings.why_it_matters: Tasks spawned inside an app's context carry that app as subject for life.
findings.recommended: A: Invert the precedence for records whose writing logger carries an owner stamp, so the owner wins.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: Level resolution ends up spread across several sources with no single resolver
findings.why_it_matters: Five level sources read in different classes; #345 would touch all of them.
findings.recommended: A: D4 names one effective-level function (the writing logger's owner, plus the subject) that every level source goes through, and documents the precedence order.
findings.chosen: A: D4 names one effective-level function (the writing logger's owner, plus the subject) that every level source goes through, and documents the precedence order.

findings.title: D5's default-name rule is computed in four places, and the ledger names only two
findings.why_it_matters: Registry fallback and test harness would keep the old naming shape.
findings.chosen: In D5 (and issue 1's text), state that the default-name rule is one function called by the AppManifest validator, model_post_init, the AppRegistry fallback and the test harness's default manifest.

findings.title: D5 checks uniqueness on instance_name, but the key that must be unique is App.unique_name
findings.why_it_matters: unique_name collides via the class-prefix rule and dotted names alias loggers.
findings.recommended: B: Keep D5's rejection of duplicate `instance_name`s across app keys, add a check that derived `unique_name`s are unique, and validate the charset of section keys and `instance_name`.
findings.chosen: Own milestone, before logging
findings.choice_reason: User asked for the first-principles fix: the user-chosen name becomes the sole instance identity (new D11), delivered as a prerequisite Instance identity milestone.

findings.title: D5-E doesn't say how a one-entry list is treated
findings.why_it_matters: A table and a one-entry list look identical after normalization.
findings.recommended: A: D5 states that the shape is decided on the raw TOML type. A table is single (section key). An array of tables is a list, and every entry must be named, even when there is only one.
findings.chosen: R: Always required (Recommended)
findings.choice_reason: User proposed requiring instance_name on every configured instance, removing shape cases and derived/typed collisions.

findings.title: Renamed default instance names change values that user code keys on
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: ~3 known users. Cache keys and event-source comparisons built from a default instance_name change silently.
findings.recommended: A: Add to issue 1's migration note that cache-key prefixes and event-source comparisons built from a default `instance_name` change value, and that setting `instance_name` explicitly keeps the old value.
findings.chosen: A: Add to issue 1's migration note that cache-key prefixes and event-source comparisons built from a default `instance_name` change value, and that setting `instance_name` explicitly keeps the old value.
findings.choice_reason: Already reflected in I1's migration note by earlier decisions (old default is no longer a valid name).

findings.title: Issue 2's client_compat handling can't catch the source_tier change
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: ~3 users. Same values, new meaning means no compat failure to ignore.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: issue 2's client_compat bullet stays, and in practice it means confirming that nothing needs an ignore entry.
findings.chosen: Moot: Finding 5-A adds a separate author field
findings.choice_reason: Resolved by the Finding 5 choice; B1 now records ignore entries for the removed log field.

findings.title: D10 adds a user config key with no stated home, add-on path, or collision handling
Findings converge on the Breakdown's blanket "Milestone B starts after Milestone A" gate
findings.why_it_matters: Breakdown orders work by milestone, not consumption; no logging issue reads issues 2-4's output and the console fix ships last.
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the Breakdown's dependency ordering before addressing Findings 2 and 3
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the Breakdown's dependency ordering before addressing Findings 2 and 3
findings.choice_reason: Re-derived: Log identity milestone first (names, identity on loggers, author field, framework verbosity, console column after identity on loggers); Instance identity re-keying follows.

findings.title: Milestone B waits on D11's re-keying (issues 2-4), which no Milestone B issue consumes
findings.why_it_matters: Three PRs of schema/route/client work sit on the critical path of every logging deliverable.
findings.recommended: A: Keep D11-F1 as the end state. Change issue 5's "After:" to issue 1, and let issues 2-4 land in parallel with or after Milestone B. State the order between issue 2's and issue 6's log-table migrations.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: The add-on console fix lands last, behind Milestone A and issue 5
findings.why_it_matters: The original #3044/#3046 complaint stays unfixed for the whole chain.
findings.recommended: A: Make issues 8 and 9 depend on issue 1 only. The column renders "subject instance name, else logger name" plus the short execution id; issue 5 adds the author marker and Phase 1 subject when it lands.
findings.chosen: Superseded by Finding 1

findings.title: D4's runtime-override tier implies stored state that PUT /logs/level doesn't have
findings.why_it_matters: Ranking a runtime override above config needs a new override store; today PUT stores nothing.
findings.recommended: A: Remove tier 1 from D4's precedence
findings.chosen: A: Remove tier 1 from D4's precedence

findings.title: One per-app framework parent logger could carry both identity and level
findings.why_it_matters: stdlib level inheritance could replace per-child levels if the lifecycle logger parented the app's children.
findings.recommended: B: Keep D2/D4 as ratified
findings.chosen: B: Keep D2/D4 as ratified

findings.title: Renaming an instance silently starts a new history, with no signal
findings.why_it_matters: Once the name is the key, a rename leaves old rows under the old name with nothing telling the user.
findings.recommended: A: Add the rename consequence to D11's Ratified acceptance and to issue 1's app-configuration docs update
findings.chosen: A: Add the rename consequence to D11's Ratified acceptance and to issue 1's app-configuration docs update
findings.choice_reason: Docs note placed on the DB re-key issue, since renames only reset history once rows key on the name.

findings.title: D9 hides framework WARNING lines (handler and job timeouts) from every log view by default
findings.why_it_matters: Timeout WARNINGs show on the console but are hidden in log views and the CLI by default.
findings.recommended: A: Keep D9 as ratified
findings.chosen: A: Keep D9 as ratified

findings.title: Seeing Hassette's detail about an app needs two switches, and nothing hints at the second
findings.why_it_matters: With framework_log_level set but the opt-in off, views look unchanged and read as 'nothing logged'.
findings.recommended: A: In D9, add an indicator next to the author control when framework lines are hidden (a count, or a static note; the issue picks). Mirror it in `hassette log` as a one-line footer.
findings.chosen: A: In D9, add an indicator next to the author control when framework lines are hidden (a count, or a static note; the issue picks). Mirror it in `hassette log` as a one-line footer.

findings.title: The identity filter has to be attached to every output path; one stamp at record creation would not
findings.why_it_matters: A future third output path could forget the filter.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a new output path outside the queue and the stream handler must attach the identity filter.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a new output path outside the queue and the stream handler must attach the identity filter.

findings.title: Issues 8 and 9 are one renderer and could ship as one PR
findings.why_it_matters: Two PRs and two docs touches for one code path.
findings.chosen: Merge issues 8 and 9 in the Breakdown into one issue, "Console identity column and compact format".

findings.title: Lifecycle-logger level change is a silent regression for the common developer setup
findings.why_it_matters: Claimed regression is #2496's intended fix, already ratified with a migration note.

findings.title: Per-app extra logger and name churn under reload leave stale levels
findings.why_it_matters: Levels are set from config on every construction, so a reused name can't keep a stale level.

findings.title: D6 is a non-decision and D10 can fold into D4
findings.why_it_matters: D10 is a capability decision on a hard-to-reverse key; D6 carries #740's close-out rationale.
